expected.doc:
# Hash table collisions
Two keys can map to the same index. The table must preserve both values.
In chaining, every table slot contains a collection of entries. When a key is inserted, its hash chooses a slot and the new pair is added to that collection. Lookup hashes the key and compares keys within the chosen collection. Open addressing stores entries in the array itself. If the chosen slot is occupied, it probes other slots using a fixed sequence until it finds an available one. Lookup follows the same sequence. A smaller load factor keeps chains and probes short. Resizing changes the capacity, so existing entries must be hashed again for the new table.

For average time, a well-distributed hash gives short chains and few probes. In the worst case many keys collide, so lookup can take O(n).
